The page asserts that the number of exchanges is O(p/K) without saying what is exchanged or why there are that many. The normalized cost pK^{\tau-1} depends on this count.

Dividing by V and using d=\Theta(p^\epsilon) gives a normalized cost p^{\epsilon\lambda'}, which equals p^{1-g_3} only if g_3=1-\epsilon\lambda'. The page states g_3=\epsilon(1-\lambda') and no step connects the two, so the reader cannot check g_3 and finds the two inconsistent.
